notes.4: This question discriminated well between candidates. Some candidates chose option B by not recognising that the atoms were isotopes of the same element.
notes.8: Knowledge of the hydrogen–oxygen fuel cell and its role in producing electrical energy was often not well recalled. A third of candidates overall chose option B.
notes.12: Nearly half of all candidates chose option D. Perhaps a confusion in the meaning of the word ‘producing’ suggested to candidates that this was a chemical rather than physical product. �PAGE�9
notes.17: This question discriminated well between candidates. Some candidates chose option D which gives an incorrect symbol for the ion produced in acidic solutions.
notes.19: The distribution of the options chosen by candidates suggests that many were guessing. Where state symbols are provided, candidates are advised to use them to help answer the question. In this question, the solid product should identify the precipitation.
notes.20: Some candidates did not recognise that the question required them to identify the transition element present in the options. They should be reminded that Group I elements generally form white solids and colourless solutions.
notes.28: This was the most strongly discriminating question on this paper. Few of the candidates that performed less well overall answered this correctly and were more likely to choose any of the other options, with the majority confusing the terms anode and cathode.
notes.30: Most candidates recalled the role of catalytic converters in the reduction of oxides of nitrogen from exhaust gases. The source of the oxygen or nitrogen to form these gases was not well recalled. Option D was the most common incorrect answer.
notes.33: This was found to be a demanding question. Most recalled the role of ultraviolet light in the reaction. Only a minority of candidates recognised the equation given in statement 3 as incorrect. Hydrogen is not a reaction product of this substitution reaction. Option C was the most common answer.
notes.34: Many candidates confused esterification with the oxidation of an alcohol and suggested option A.
notes.36: Recall of the properties of these polymers was poor. Many candidates did not recall that nylon is a polyamide and will therefore produce more than two different compounds when completely combusted. Some candidates appeared to be guessing. Option B was the most common answer.
notes.37: Candidates who performed less well overall were more likely to choose any of the other options in preference to the correct answer, not identifying either the correct reactant or excluding carbon monoxide as an incorrect reaction product.
notes.39: The state symbols were not used by some candidates to identify the solid and so they did not choose filtration as a suitable separation method. Option C was the most common incorrect answer. �PAGE�10
notes.general_comments:
Overall, candidates found this to be an accessible paper. Questions 1, 3, 6 and 26 had the lowest demand
and Questions 8, 12, 19, 33, 34 and 36 had the highest demand. Many questions showed strong
discrimination between candidates. Candidates should take care to read each option carefully so that any
partially correct answers can be excluded.
